scientific_target.question: How accurately can permitted cue/reward history predict released fluorescence trajectories on complete held-out reward-spacing conditions, with biological aliases grouped and a separately identified cue-time forecast condition?
scientific_target.known_answer: The stored, processed photometry fluorescence samples at the exact observed native timestamps for each eligible held-out event trajectory. These measurements, not the paper narrative or a fitted baseline curve, define the target.
scientific_target.answer_origin: Author NWB processing/photometry/photometry_dff and its timestamps, joined to verified event logs; all current source outcomes are exposed development material.
scientific_target.case_unit: An eligible complete event trajectory nested in session and verified biological animal; historical source-ID scope has 2691 clock-complete trajectories.
scientific_target.independent_unit: Verified biological animal; the 13 historical source IDs cannot be assumed independent across naming families until aliases are resolved.
scientific_target.inference_scope: Retrospective encoding of released fluorescence across source conditions. Actual reward alignment and upstream whole-session processing preclude a real-time or raw-signal comprehension claim. Dopamine-specific attribution requires verified anatomy and missed-fiber exclusions.
exclusions: No claim that reference-relative skill is ordinary variance-based R-squared.
No independent-cohort replication across NEURAL-045, NEURAL-046 or PAPER-FIND-044.
No transfer of historical two-condition results to six-condition appetitive or aversive full-programme coverage.

inputs: Permitted training fluorescence trajectories and native timestamps, plus verified cue/reward history, condition, session/day and declared nuisance variables.

Historical transfer covers 60-second and 600-second source cohorts; the prospective full programme separates six photometry-designated appetitive conditions from two aversive conditions and excludes behavior-only conditions from neural target creation.

primary.name: Equal-animal mean native-time prediction skill relative to current canonical R0, with native MSE retained
primary.aggregation: Integrate squared error over each observed native span using physical-time quadrature, average trajectories within each verified animal, then compute the unweighted animal mean of 1 minus candidate MSE divided by that animal's independently registered current R0 MSE. Current central comparison source fixes canonical_denominator to R0. Historical 2691-trajectory scores instead divide by original T native MSE and remain a distinct named comparison.
primary.rationale: Measures prediction of held-out measured trajectories without allowing dense sampling or prolific source IDs to dominate. This is reference-relative skill, not variance R-squared. Missing current R0 makes the primary required-unscorable even when native MSE is available; any zero R0 denominator makes the primary undefined without clipping or dropping that animal. Historical T and current R0 are different references, so their relative-skill values are not interchangeable.

secondary: Native-time MSE, MAE and signed bias in stored fluorescence units, reported per animal and condition.
Both transfer directions, complete exclusions and endpoint support; equal-session and sex/hardware/outcome/early-trial diagnostics.
